scenes.text: Here's a thought. Every single day, millions of people film themselves doing things. Cooking dinner. Fixing a machine. Building a computer. So what if a computer could watch just one of those videos, and actually learn the skill?
That's EIDOS. Show it once, and it turns the video into a skill it can check.
First, it watches. It picks out every step, the order they need to happen in, and what the finished result should look like. It's like writing a recipe, straight from the video.
Then, it watches you. Through any camera, it follows along in real time. It knows which step you're on, and it tells you what comes next.
And if you miss something? It stops you. Right then. Not after.
It isn't just for people, either. Show a robot arm the task once, and it can do it, and check its own work. Knock the stack over, and it notices. Then it fixes it.
EIDOS is built on Meta's AI models, for the Meta Global AI Hackathon.
Made by Maruthi Kunchala, with Team Pulse Parallax. EIDOS. Show it once.
